title: FactBank: a corpus annotated with event factuality
research_question: How can event factuality be represented and reliably annotated as source-relative combinations of polarity and epistemic certainty in text?
methodology: The authors define event factuality as the commitment of relevant discourse sources toward the factual status of events and construct a discrete annotation framework combining polarity with degrees of epistemic certainty. FactBank adds this semantic layer to TimeBank and a subset of the AQUAINT TimeML corpus, yielding 208 documents and 9,488 manually annotated events. Annotation is decomposed into identifying source-introducing predicates, identifying relevant sources, and assigning factuality values, with copredication-based diagnostic tests used to distinguish modality levels. Inter-annotator agreement is measured separately for the three annotation tasks.

key_findings.finding: FactBank contains 208 documents and 9,488 manually annotated events drawn from TimeBank and a subset of the AQUAINT TimeML corpus.

The factuality representation combines positive, negative, or underspecified polarity with certain, probable, possible, or underspecified modality, thereby distinguishing facts, counterfacts, uncertainty, and non-commitment.

Inter-annotator agreement was high for the annotation decomposition: Cohen's kappa was 0.88 for source-introducing predicates, 0.95 for source identification, and 0.81 for factuality-value assignment.
The corpus explicitly represents factuality relative to relevant sources rather than treating factuality as a single source-independent truth value.
The annotation deliberately excludes factuality changes that require multiple sentences, even though the authors note that an initially uncommitted event may later be presented as a fact.
The AQUAINT portion is strongly skewed: 58.1% of annotated values are certain-positive and 36.6% are fully underspecified, while lower-certainty or non-positive categories are comparatively rare.

limitations: Factuality judgments are intentionally constrained to sentence-level information, so cross-sentence revisions and state changes are not annotated.
FactBank contains English news-style material rather than workplace email or dialogue.
The annotation represents textual source commitment, not independent verification that an event actually occurred.
Rare probable, possible, and negative factuality categories produce a highly imbalanced label distribution.
The framework does not directly encode operational lifecycle states such as planned, scheduled, completed, revoked, superseded, or reopened.
A discourse model for tracking changing factuality across sentences is identified as necessary but is outside the corpus annotation design.
raw_claims: Event factuality is defined in terms of a source's commitment toward the factual nature of an event.
Factuality varies along polarity and certainty dimensions.
The scheme distinguishes certain, probable, possible, and underspecified modality.
FactBank contains 208 documents and 9,488 manually annotated events.
FactBank is layered on top of existing TimeML-annotated material.
Annotation first identifies source-introducing predicates and relevant sources before assigning factuality.
Cohen's kappa for factuality-value assignment is 0.81.
An event can be introduced without commitment and later be characterized as factual in subsequent discourse.
The released annotation nevertheless restricts factuality judgments to the containing sentence.
Certain-positive and fully underspecified values dominate the AQUAINT portion of the corpus.
The authors state that FactBank is to be made available through the Linguistic Data Consortium.
